description: ol-reserved-word (issue #837, maintainer ruling #833): the boundaries of binding, given that binding a built-in name is unconditionally free (spec/grammar.md:365, :390). It pins two boundaries: (1) `:count = 3` (the Core primitive `count`) and `:helper = 4` (a procedure declared in this same program) are bindings, and spec/grammar.md:410 keeps variables out of the one callable namespace primitives, user procedures, and struct constructors share, so they shadow nothing; (2) a write INTO an existing value introduces no name, so `:repeat[1] = 5` on line 8 is data, not a declaration -- spec/grammar.md:408, "a postfix names a field or key, which is data". `"check": true` (semantic-checker only) -- nothing is executed and no events are produced.
